findings.section: Why this shape / S1 / S2 / S3
findings.summary: `--version` can deliberately install an older binary, but S2's unversioned plugin update commands can leave or install newer plugins, contradicting the promise that self-update updates the binary and plugin together.
findings.evidence: The brief explicitly permits `--version <v>` to install an older version at lines 69-74, then requires every found plugin to run its unversioned latest-marketplace update at lines 155-178; S3 line 213 says self-update updates "the binary and the plugin". For example, `--version v0.14.0` from v0.15.0 can roll the binary back while the plugin remains or updates to v0.15.0.
findings.fix: The operator must choose and pin the semantics: skip plugin updates with `--version`, update plugins independently and disclose a possible version mismatch, or support a version-pinning mechanism for each agent. Then align S1/S2, the S3 doctor wording, the JSON contract, the worked downgrade example, and acceptance.

findings.summary: `--check` exits before the contract has resolved `dir`, although the JSON document always requires a `dir` and the safety contract says a binary outside the Go install directory is refused.
findings.evidence: S1 step 4 at lines 121-129 prints and exits for `--check`; S1 step 6 at lines 132-137 resolves the install directory and checks the executable path. The `--json` contract at lines 194-205 still requires `dir` in the one document.
findings.fix: Define the `--check` order explicitly. If it performs the normal safety checks, resolve and validate the install directory before the step-4 exit and pin the refusal outputs; otherwise define a literal `dir` value for an unqueried or unavailable install location and amend the safety claim.

findings.section: S2 / The update commands / Binding references
findings.summary: The Claude update command's scoped syntax relies on external CLI help that is neither captured in the repository nor cited by a repository-relative binding reference.
findings.evidence: Lines 166-168 prescribe `claude plugin update vloop@vloop --scope <scope>` and attribute it to `claude plugin update --help` on 2026-11-26. The binding references contain no in-repository record of that help output, while `.vloop/repo-guidelines.md` requires external formats and flags to be taken from the tool or its docs.
findings.fix: Record the relevant help output and plugin-list fixture in `docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md` or another cited repository document, then bind this brief to that entry. Do the same for Copilot's update syntax if it is not already covered by the cited predecessor.

findings.summary: The `message` value for failed plugin list, marketplace, and update cases is not literal, so a JSON gate cannot know whether it should compare the last tool-output line or the full prefixed human-readable warning.
findings.evidence: Lines 172-184 define several different exact human lines for failures, while lines 201-205 say only that `message` carries "the failure's line". The worked example includes the human line at lines 281-282 but no `--json` failure document.
findings.fix: Pin one JSON object for each distinct failed case, including the exact `message` string, or state and demonstrate that `message` is exactly the corresponding human line without its severity prefix; add those objects to the worked example.

findings.summary: The B44 roadmap row required at brief handover is absent.
findings.evidence: The brief names itself B44 at line 10, but `docs/design-notes/vloop-roadmap-b18-b21.md` ends its rows at B41 at line 48. `.claude/skills/vloop-architect/SKILL.md` lines 17-19 requires the roadmap row to point at the brief at handover.
findings.fix: Add B44 with its owned slice and dependency to the applicable roadmap, or update the roadmap heading/range and ownership row in the same ready commit.

decisions: The command is `vloop self-update`; `vloop upgrade` continues to mean repository upgrade. This separation is sound.
Go's module tool is the release channel: `go list -m -json ...@latest` outside a module, then `go install .../cmd/vloop@<version>`. This avoids a second release channel.
Without `--version`, only strictly newer releases are installed; `--version` explicitly allows an older or pre-release target. The plugin consequence of this override is not settled.
The command refuses when Go is absent, the module version is devel, or the executable is not in Go's install directory. Sound as a safety boundary; `--check` ordering still needs definition.
Doctor and `vloop upgrade` remain offline. Sound.
A plugin update failure is reported but non-fatal after the binary step. Sound, provided the final status is explicit in JSON and prose.

Add the C-2 path exception for machine-wide binaries and install directories, rendering them with `/` and `~`. Sound, but the implementation must also normalize tool-derived path text where it is printed.
Tests use temporary Go-program fakes for Go and both agents, use `x/mod/semver`, and `--check` with `--version` compares the exact target. These are sound test mechanics.
